In triangle $ABC$, angle $B$ is a right angle. Point $D$ lies on side $AC$ such that $BD$ is perpendicular to $AC$. If $AD = 3$ and $DC = 12$, what is the value of $C$?
explanation: Choice A is correct. When an altitude is drawn from the right angle to the hypotenuse of a right triangle, it creates geometric mean relationships. The hypotenuse $AC = AD + DC = 3 + 12 = 15$. Using the geometric mean relationship, $AB^2 = AD \cdot AC = 3 \cdot 15 = 45$, so $AB = \sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}$. Similarly, $BC^2 = DC \cdot AC = 12 \cdot 15 = 180$, so $BC = 6\sqrt{5}$. In right triangle $ABC$, $\sin C = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{15} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}$.
